# A complete seven-fiber obstruction to the reflected density-allocation envelope

This note tests a precise sufficient-certificate family. At each integer
base it permits every disjoint reflected pair, every fractional endpoint
allocation, and even the best possible universal lower bound which remembers
only the OWN volume, the SUM midpoint mass, and the SUM density ceiling at
the prescribed centroid of own volume plus twice the midpoint measure.
It also permits every individual fiber centroid.

The certificate fails on an actual convex body in every integer rank n>=1,
with continuous dimension d=2 and seven fibers per binary block. This is
not an OC counterexample and not an obstruction to all coupling constructions
or all choices of center. In particular the stronger directional marginal
shape and the actual common midpoint support are deliberately not encoded
by this scalar envelope.

## 1. The exact scalar envelope being tested

For d>=1, L>=0 and 0<=alpha<=L define

    beta_d(L,alpha) = inf_(F,eta) D_(1_F dx+eta)(g_(1_F dx+2eta)),        (1)

where F ranges over d-dimensional convex bodies of volume ONE,
eta ranges over measurable measures with 0<=eta<=L1_F dx and
eta(F)=alpha, g denotes the ordinary vector centroid of the indicated
measure, and D_nu(y) is the raw halfspace depth

    D_nu(y)=inf_{H closed halfspace containing y} nu(H).

The outer infimum need not be attained for this definition or any argument
below. Every upper bound we use is supplied by an explicit admissible F,eta
and an actual closed halfspace containing its specified centroid. For L=0
only alpha=0 is allowed; ordinary Grunbaum and a simplex give
beta_d(0,0)=Gamma_d.

Fix an actual positive fiber K_p of volume k, and enumerate all unordered
distinct reflected pairs {z,w}, z+w=2p, with positive endpoint volumes
a_j,b_j. Set

    B_j=((a_j^(1/d)+b_j^(1/d))/2)^d,
    0<=t_j<=min(a_j,b_j),
    T=sum_j t_j,  L=sum_j t_j/B_j,  alpha=T/k.          (2)

Convexity and BM give B_j<=k, hence alpha<=L. Distinct reflected pairs
use disjoint endpoints. Their conditional-transport midpoint measures
sum to an actual eta with mass T and density at most L on K_p. At
the actual source g_(1_Kp dx+2eta), every ambient halfspace captures
at least its own-fiber cap plus eta's middle cap. These facts, including
all oblique normals and boundary masses, are proved in
`candidate 21545f87e4705da7`.

After volume normalization, the strongest guarantee which uses ONLY
this scalar density-ceiling information at that prescribed source is
k beta_d(L,alpha). The enlarged certificate family tested here is

    E_p=max{Gamma_d k,
            sup_(all allocations in (2)) k beta_d(L,alpha)},
    E=max_(actual positive bases p) E_p.              (3)

The no-pair allocation already includes the ordinary own-fiber term;
it is displayed to make the individual-centroid option explicit.
Every universal scalar bound in terms of (L,alpha) at this same source
is no larger than beta by definition. Thus (3) dominates the stated
b_d(L,alpha) saturation certificate, the capacity-one dominated-centroid
bounds, the single-pair theta-gain formula, and the planar c_* bound.
Those bounds cannot evade an upper bound on (3) by choosing a different
allocation or integer base. Pure integer caps do not affect this comparison:
the allocated contribution there is at least k+T, whereas the upper
bounds on beta below never exceed Gamma_d(1+alpha)<=1+alpha.

This definition does NOT optimize arbitrary center-dependent functionals,
does not retain separate geometric information about the eta_j after they
are added, and does not assert that every test measure in (1) is a midpoint
measure of the original fibers. It is deliberately an upper envelope of
all universal guarantees from the TOTAL ceiling and TOTAL mass only.

## 2. Two universal upper tests for the scalar envelope

For all d,L,alpha in its domain,

    beta_d(L,alpha)<=Gamma_d(1+alpha).                 (4)

Indeed take F to be any volume-one simplex and eta=alpha 1_F dx,
which is admissible since alpha<=L. The indicated source is its
centroid, and one ordinary simplex centroid cap has volume Gamma_d.
The captured 1_F+eta mass is exactly Gamma_d(1+alpha).

The following sharper planar test will handle the central base. Suppose
0<=alpha<=7/8 and L>=L_min(alpha), where

    L_min(alpha)=16alpha/9                 for 0<=alpha<=9/16,
                  4alpha-5/4               for 9/16<=alpha<=13/16,
                  16alpha-11              for 13/16<=alpha<=7/8.

Then

    beta_2(L,alpha)<=136/225.                         (5)

For alpha<=9/25 this follows from (4), since
(4/9)(1+9/25)=136/225. For the rest of the range we give an exact
two-band simplex measure and a finite polynomial certificate.

Let F be a triangle of area one with apex height one and opposite
edge height zero. Its upper-cap volume at height x is (1-x)^2.
For X uniform in F, the rank variable v=(1-x)^2 is uniform on [0,1],
and x=1-sqrt(v). Put

    s=4/9,  r=4/25,  l=L_min(alpha),

and define eta to have density l on the two rank bands

    [0,r/l] and [s, s+(alpha-r)/l],                   (6)

and zero elsewhere. For alpha>=9/25 all these quantities are defined;
the two bands are disjoint up to endpoints and lie in [0,1]. Explicitly
r<=l s and alpha-r<=l(1-s). These linear inequalities can be checked
at the endpoints of each of the three cells, because l is affine on
each cell. Thus eta has mass alpha and density at most l<=L.

The closed cap x>=1/3 has F-volume s and eta-mass r, hence objective
mass s+r=136/225. It remains to verify that it contains the centroid
of 1_F+2eta. Since the uniform projected mean is 1/3, this is exactly
the inequality

    integral sqrt(v) d eta <= (2/3)alpha.             (7)

Integrating over (6) and multiplying by 3sqrt(l)/2 shows (7) is
equivalent to

    J sqrt(l) >= 8/125+R^(3/2),
    J=alpha+8l/27,   R=alpha+4l/9-4/25.              (8)

All J,l,R are positive on the three intervals considered. Define

    C=l J^2-R^3-64/15625,
    P=15625 C^2-256 R^3.                             (9)

If C>0 and P>0, then C>(16/125)R^(3/2), which gives
l J^2>(R^(3/2)+8/125)^2 and proves (8) strictly. The following
explicit polynomial identities certify both strict inequalities.

## 3. Complete rational certificates for the three cells

For each cell let alpha=a+(b-a)t, 0<=t<=1, and use the corresponding
affine l above. Write B_(i,m)(t)=binom(m,i)t^i(1-t)^(m-i).
The arrays below mean the exact identities

    C(alpha)=sum_(i=0)^3 c_i B_(i,3)(t)/D_C,
    P(alpha)=sum_(i=0)^6 p_i B_(i,6)(t)/D_P.          (10)

All listed denominators and every listed numerator are strictly positive.
The Bernstein basis is nonnegative and sums to one, so these identities
prove C>0 and P>0 on the full CLOSED cells, including every seam.

Cell I: a=9/25, b=9/16, l=16alpha/9.

    D_C = 1728000000
    c = [130551808, 171470080, 208093840, 217571125]
    D_P = 63700992000000
    p = [3827222456565760, 4914205160374272, 6053671353909248,
         7054618243919872, 7605056558783232, 7304723224946672,
         5871864781021267]

Cell II: a=9/16, b=13/16, l=4alpha-5/4.

    D_C = 41472000
    c = [5221707, 7729927, 10396147, 11708367]
    D_P = 573308928000000
    p = [52846783029191403, 84506377766468903, 125555527202496403,
         171282187512273903, 209151434370801403, 217561212953078903,
         176505087934106403]

Cell III: a=13/16, b=7/8, l=16alpha-11.

    D_C = 207360000
    c = [58541835, 84637138, 116080716, 152551944]
    D_P = 573308928000000
    p = [176505087934106403, 406383027911818978, 735845417463840428,
         1189713577869805128, 1795687102216769328, 2583986607342570528,
         3587017902527233728]

These are polynomial identities in one variable, so the tables can also
be verified simply by expansion of (9). They are a proof for every
real allocation parameter in the cells, not sampled numerical evidence.
This completes (5).

## 4. An actual seven-fiber convex body

Choose any area-one triangle T with centroid zero and one vertex P.
In R x R^2, first take the convex hull of {-4}x{P}, {0}xT,
and {4}x{P}, and then intersect it with -3<=z<=3. Call the result C_1.
It is a compact full-dimensional convex body. Its exact fiber at any
real z in [-3,3] is

    K_z=(1-|z|/4)T+(|z|/4)P.                         (11)

For example, when z>=0, a convex combination of an apex at +4 with
T gives the stated copy. Allowing the opposite apex cannot enlarge
it: such a combination has total weight on the apices at least z/4,
and the copies (1-t)T+tP are nested as t increases because P belongs
to T. The case z<=0 is identical. This proves (11) for the full convex
hull, rather than only exhibiting a subset of each fiber.

The complete integer base is {-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3}; all seven fibers
have positive area. Their areas and centroids are

    V_z=(1-|z|/4)^2,
    g_z=(|z|/4)P.

The centroid graph is genuinely nonaffine, since P!=0. The total
original mixed area is

    M=1+2(9/16+1/4+1/16)=11/4.                       (12)

No unsampled fibers are inserted into the measure, and no original
positive fiber is dropped from M.

At the central base p=0, there are exactly three reflected pairs,
with equal endpoint areas

    B_1=9/16, B_2=1/4, B_3=1/16.

For every allocation t_j<=B_j, alpha=T is at most 7/8 and
L=sum_j t_j/B_j. Minimizing L at fixed T fills the largest B_j first:
if a smaller B carries positive allocation while a larger B is not
full, shifting a small amount to the larger B strictly decreases L.
Repeating gives exactly the three-cell function L_min in Section 2.
This is an attained finite linear allocation problem, not a relaxation
assuming the pair masses can be reassigned to a different base.
Hence (5) applies to EVERY central allocation and gives

    E_0<=136/225.                                    (13)

For an integer p with 1<=p<=3, every reflected pair is {p-h,p+h}
with 1<=h<=3-p. Its smaller endpoint area is V_(p+h), because
|p+h|>=|p-h|. Consequently, for any allocation,

    k+T<=sum_(j=p)^3 V_j<=9/16+1/4+1/16=7/8.

Using the uniform test (4), we obtain

    E_p<=(4/9)(7/8)=7/18.                            (14)

The same bound holds for p<0 by base reflection. The no-pair cases
p=+/-3 and every own-fiber centroid are included. Combining (13)--(14),

    E<=136/225 < 11/18 = (Gamma_2/2) M,
    (Gamma_2/2)M-E >=1/150.                          (15)

Thus even the enlarged scalar envelope (3) fails at EVERY integer
anchor, after optimization over the continuum of all allowed pair
allocations. This does not estimate the actual best depth from above.

## 5. The same failure in every integer rank

For any n>=1 form the actual convex body

    C_n=[0,1]^(n-1) x C_1

with the first n coordinates interpreted as integer coordinates.
The complete integer base is {0,1}^(n-1) x {-3,...,3}, and every
fiber is the corresponding actual triangle (11). If two binary
vectors have integer midpoint equal to another binary vector, they
are identical coordinate by coordinate. Therefore every reflected
pair at a base (e,p) remains in the SAME binary block e, and the
full scalar allocation menu there is exactly the one already audited.
No new cross-block pairs appear in higher rank.

The total original mass is M_n=2^(n-1)(11/4), and its OC target is

    Gamma_2 M_n/2^n=11/18.

Thus the upper bound 136/225 and the same exact gap 1/150 in (15)
hold for the certificate at every base, in every n>=1. The body has
ambient interior, all integer fibers are full-dimensional, and no
lattice transformation or change of Hausdorff normalization is used.

## 6. What this does and does not exclude

The obstruction includes all the explicitly stated lower formulas
which use total midpoint mass and total density ceiling at the
centroid of own volume plus twice that midpoint measure. It even
allows a hypothetical optimal theorem using just those parameters,
since beta is defined by their full universal infimum. It also
includes the ordinary own-fiber Grunbaum option and arbitrary choice
of integer anchor, while always comparing to the ORIGINAL M_n.

It does not include an arbitrary optimized continuous center, separate
directional shape constraints on actual midpoint couplings, individual
component density/mass constraints retained beyond their sums, a joint
common-midpoint-support theorem, or direct cap credits from unpaired
fibers. The two-band eta used to upper-bound beta is not claimed to
be realizable by the original endpoint bodies. That distinction is
why (15) is an obstruction to a scalar sufficient certificate and
not an OC counterexample. The earlier complete-midpoint-star and
covariogram-selector obstructions concern different certificates;
none of their conclusions is used in this proof.

There is also an explicit independently certified good point in the
original example. In one binary block take Y with chain base zero
and continuous coordinate P/4. Its two neighbors at bases -1,+1
are the same body F=(3/4)T+P/4, of area 9/16 and centroid P/4;
the own body T contains F. For every nonvertical through-Y halfspace,
ordinary Grunbaum pays Gamma_2|F| from the contained own copy, and
the proved ordinary paired-centroid-tail theorem pays 2Gamma_2|F|
from the two identical neighboring fibers, at their opposite ambient
threshold shifts. This is the theorem proved in
`candidate 732b11a769399016`, used only
for one identical pair. Thus the ORIGINAL mixed raw depth at Y is
at least 3Gamma_2(9/16)=3/4, exceeding 11/18 by 5/36. A pure
integer cap contains the own fiber and at least one neighboring
fiber, so is larger still. Translating a containing boundary through
Y preserves the lower bound; other binary blocks only add mass.
This verifies OC for this example independently of the failed
scalar envelope and makes no appeal to a conjectural global theorem.
